central_question: As of 30 June 2027, will the EU definitive countervailing duties on Chinese battery-electric vehicles (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, up to 35.3% on top of the 10% tariff) remain in force unchanged, be replaced by a negotiated price-undertaking or minimum-price agreement, or otherwise be altered — and will China take retaliatory measures against EU automotive exports before that date?

situation_brief.current_situation: EU definitive countervailing duties of 7.8%–35.3% (BYD 17.0%, Geely 18.8%, SAIC 35.3%, Tesla Shanghai 7.8%, cooperating 20.7%, residual 35.3%) have applied since 30 October 2024 for five years (expiry 31 October 2029). One company-specific undertaking from Volkswagen (Anhui), accepted 9–10 February 2026 via Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/330, exempts that exporter; all others remain dutied. WTO dispute DS630 panel was composed 13 October 2025; final report not expected before Q2 2027; both parties pre-agreed MPIA-style Article 25 appeal arbitration on 31 July 2025.
situation_brief.context: China's WTO challenge (consultations 4 November 2024, panel established 25 April 2025) runs parallel to negotiations: minimum-price talks restarted December 2025, Commission undertaking guidance issued 12 January 2026, and a 9 October 2026 EU-China understanding caps Chinese hybrid exports (~350,000/year over four years via a safeguard with provisionals advertised for December 2026) and commits to 'immediately begin negotiations on electric vehicle price undertakings'. China has imposed calibrated retaliation: final brandy duties up to 34.9% (from 5 July 2025) with minimum-price exemptions for major cognac houses, final pork duties 4.9%–19.8% (from 17 December 2025), dairy finals reported at 7.4%–11.7% after provisionals of 21.9%–42.7%.
situation_brief.dynamics: The five-year expiry clock does not bind before the horizon; no expiry-review decision point falls before 30 June 2027. The February 2026 VW (Anhui) precedent shows a ~9-week review cycle for accepting new undertakings. The DS630 report barely overlaps the horizon, and appeal arbitration would push resolution past it. China's retaliation pattern is calibrated and reversible, with final rates set well below provisionals and linked to EV-talk progress (Reuters reported cognac relief conditioned on EV-tariff progress). German politics shifted from opposing duties (2024) to joining France in pressing for stronger trade defence (Merz–Macron letter, 2026).
fault_lines: Commission openness to undertakings vs its doubt that a single minimum price would counter subsidy-caused injury
MOFCOM's insistence on government-to-government negotiation vs the Commission's company-specific undertaking model
French protectionist coalition vs German OEM exposure to Chinese retaliation (~1/3 of 2023 German car sales in China)
Chinese exporters' discount-driven volume strategies vs undertaking minimum prices and quotas
WTO legal challenge vs Commission defence of its instrument
